messages.author: 8fc2bc9cca049463
messages.subject: Probit function?
parts: Is there a Probit function in stan? I need to get quantiles from a normal distribution, but all I seem to find are the normal cdf and erf rather than their inverses. Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Probit function?
parts:
On 7/9/13 11:46 AM, kris2...@gmail.com wrote:
> Is there a Probit function in stan? I need to get quantiles from a normal distribution, but all I seem to find are the
> normal cdf and erf rather than their inverses. Thanks

Section 11.4 of the manual explains how to do logit and
probit GLMs. And 11.3 is on robit :-)

You have both Phi and the normal CDF. Phi will be a bit
more efficient and more idiomatic, so it's what we used
in the manual examples.

- Bob

messages.author: 8fc2bc9cca049463
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Probit function?
parts: I'm not doing probit regression though. And it seems that Phi will give me the cdf (i.e. P < x ), but I need the inverse cdf. So, and forgive me for being ignorant here, let's say all I need is the 0.95 quantile of the normal distribution with mean mu and sd sigma, what function will spit out the quantile?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Probit function?

> I'm not doing probit regression though. And it seems that Phi will give me the cdf (i.e. P < x ), but I need the
> inverse cdf. So, and forgive me for being ignorant here, let's say all I need is the 0.95 quantile of the normal
> distribution with mean mu and sd sigma, what function will spit out the quantile?

Sorry --- I misunderstood your question.

We don't have inverse CDFs yet. They're on our
to-do list. These functions are tricky for Stan
because we need derivatives w.r.t. all the arguments
for full generality in our modeling language.

- Bob
